name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
symptoms: Sometimes cloudy urine or blood in urine
classes: Antibiotic selection requires clinical assessment; examples of classes/agents used in selected lower UTIs include nitrofurantoin and fosfomycin. They are not suitable for every UTI or kidney infection.
tests: Urine culture and sensitivity when indicated
precautions: Do not start, repeat, share, or stop antibiotics without an authorized prescriber.
Pregnancy, allergy, kidney function, culture results and local resistance patterns affect treatment.
refer: Fever/chills, flank or back pain, vomiting
Pregnancy, child, male patient, recurrent UTI or kidney disease
Blood in urine, inability to urinate, confusion or severe weakness

name: Fever
classes: Fever is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Symptom-relief medicines must be selected with age, weight, allergies, other medicines and liver/kidney history in mind.
tests: Tests depend on cause, duration, age and examination; not every fever needs the same tests.
precautions: Record temperature, duration and accompanying symptoms.
Do not use adult products or doses for children.
Antibiotics are not routine treatment for viral infections.
refer: Breathing difficulty, confusion, seizure, dehydration or severe weakness
Infant, pregnancy, immune compromise, persistent or worsening fever

name: Common cold and cough
classes: Most common colds are viral. Symptom-relief product classes differ; age, other conditions and duplicate ingredients must be checked.
tests: Often clinical assessment; testing depends on symptoms and risk.
precautions: Antibiotics do not routinely treat common colds.
Avoid duplicate ingredients in combination products.
Do not give cough/cold medicines to young children without clinician advice.
refer: Shortness of breath, chest pain, dehydration
Worsening asthma or other serious chronic illness

name: Acidity / heartburn
symptoms: Burning behind the breastbone, often after meals
classes: Antacids, alginates, H2 blockers and proton-pump inhibitors are different classes; suitability depends on symptoms, duration, other medicines and medical history.
tests: Persistent or recurrent symptoms may need clinical evaluation.
refer: Chest pain/pressure with sweating or breathlessness: emergency assessment
Difficulty swallowing, unexplained weight loss, repeated vomiting, black stool or blood

name: Diarrhoea
classes: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) helps prevent dehydration. Anti-diarrhoeal medicines are not suitable for everyone; antibiotics are used only for selected causes under clinical direction.
tests: Testing may be considered for severe, prolonged or bloody diarrhoea.
precautions: Prepare ORS exactly as the packet instructs.
Avoid self-treatment when there is blood in stool or fever.
refer: Blood in stool, severe abdominal pain or high fever
Very little urine, dizziness, lethargy or signs of dehydration
Infant, older adult, pregnancy or persistent symptoms
